sentences.text: 1 2 . By this petition filed under Article 226 and 227 of the Constitution of India, the petitioners question the legality of order dated 2/4 29.wp.3473.22-J.odt 23.11.2021 passed by the respondent No.2, which was communicated to the petitioner by letter dated 03.12.2021, whereby the respondent No.2 rejected the application filed under Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the L.A.Act").

The land of the petitioners under Gat No.17, admeasuring 10 hectares of village Nimba, Taluqua Digras, District Yavatmal was acquired for Savanga Punarvasan Project on Digras - Arni Highway Road in Land Acquisition Proceedings No.2/47/83-84.
3.
The petitioners did not seek reference under Section 18 of the L. A. Act.

One Raheman, whose land was also acquired under the same notification, had filed a reference under Section 18 of the L.
A. Act, which was registered as Land Acquisition Case No. 151/2006 (Raheman Vs. State) before Civil Judge Senior Division, Darwha.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Case No. 151/2006 (Raheman Vs. State)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The reference Court, by judgment dated 29.09.2015, partly allowed the reference and enhanced the compensation to Rs.3.80 per Square Feet.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of the compensation awarded by the reference Court, said Raheman has filed appeal under Section 54 of the L. A. Act, which was stated to be pending before this Court.

The petitioners claim that they were not aware of the award passed in Land Acquisition Case No.151/2006 and that it was only when said Raheman informed them about the judgment that he applied for the certified copy on 12.09.2021.
He received the certified copy on 01.10.2021 and filed an application 3/4 29.wp.3473.22-J.odt under Section 28A of the L. A. Act on 18.10.2021.

By the impugned order dated 23.11.2021, the Land Acquisition Officer has rejected the application under Section 28A of the L. A.
Act mainly on the ground of the delay.
Learned Assistant Government Pleader supports the decision on the ground that the application was filed beyond the prescribed period of limitation.
4. The learned Counsel for the petitioners states that the said order was passed without affording an opportunity of hearing.
It is pertinent to note that Sub-Section 2 of Section 28A of the L. A. Act contemplates an opportunity of hearing and an inquiry.
The affidavit-in- reply filed on behalf of the respondent Nos. 1 and 2, does not indicate that the petitioners were given an opportunity of hearing.

In these circumstances, the impugned order which is in reach of the principle of natural justice,
cannot be sustained.
5. Hence, the impugned order dated 23.11.2021 is quashed and set aside.
6. The respondent No.2 - Land Acquisition Officer is directed to hear the petitioners and decide the application afresh in accordance with law.
Rule is made absolute in above terms.
No order as to costs.
(MRS. VRUSHALI V. JOSHI, J.)

(SMT. ANUJA PRABHUDESSAI, J.) RGurnule.
